claims.text: For historical context: the two-state solution used to be the US's official position. It was the framework of Oslo, Camp David, and every US-brokered negotiation for 30 years. The fact that a UNGA resolution affirming what was once American policy now gets vetoed tells you how far the political landscape has shifted. The international consensus hasn't changed — the US position has.

claims.text: The UNGA vote is symbolically powerful but practically limited. General Assembly resolutions aren't binding, and the US veto at the Security Council means Palestinian statehood through the UN remains blocked regardless of how many countries support it. That said, the 143-9 margin is striking — it demonstrates how isolated the US-Israel position is on this issue globally. The diplomatic trajectory is clear even if the political mechanism is stuck.
